title: Binary Search
description: Given an array of integers nums which is sorted in ascending order, and an integer target, write a function to search target in nums. If target exists, return its index; otherwise return -1.
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order
hints: Because the array is sorted, you can discard half the search space at every step.
Watch out for infinite loops from off-by-one errors when choosing mid.
solution_approach: Initialize two pointers lo and hi around the whole array. While lo <= hi, take mid = lo + (hi - lo) // 2, compare nums[mid] to target, and narrow the search window accordingly.
common_mistakes: Off-by-one in the loop condition causing an infinite loop or missing an element.
Using mid = (lo + hi) // 2 which can overflow for very large arrays in lower-level languages (prefer lo + (hi-lo)//2).
similar_problems: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array

brute_force.description: Scan the whole array linearly until the target is found.

better.description: Classic binary search: repeatedly halve the search space using a while loop with inclusive bounds.

optimal.description: Recursive binary search is equivalent in time but consumes O(log N) stack space, so the iterative version is preferred.
